ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a transition-state-style molecular skeleton; on the left there is a cyclic/chain skeleton containing double bonds and curved arrows are drawn; the key carbon atom on the right is connected to the OSiR3 substituent above, the R' substituent at the lower right, and two unsaturated carbon-chain fragments on the left. The problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: According to the specified reading, take the substituted carbon on the right as the central carbon; R' is represented by the wildcard atom *; the upper-left two-carbon unsaturated branch is encoded as C=C; the lower-left three-carbon unsaturated branch is encoded as CC=C; the oxygen-silicon substituent is encoded as O[Si](*)(*)*. Connecting these substituents to the central carbon gives the SMILES: *C(C=C)(CC=C)O[Si](*)(*)*.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: Read the molecular graph in the image while ignoring the curved arrows. Treat the right-hand substituted carbon as the central atom. Encode its four substituents: R' as '*', the upper-left unsaturated two-carbon branch as C=C, the lower-left three-carbon branch as CC=C, and the oxygen-silyl substituent as O[Si](*)(*)*. Combine these substituents around the central carbon in SMILES form, giving *C(C=C)(CC=C)O[Si](*)(*)*.

planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to know the requested output format is a SMILES expression and that the arrows in the image must be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use line-angle conventions: unlabeled vertices are carbons with implied hydrogens; R/R' substituents are represented as wildcard atoms '*'; the silyl ether is written as O[Si](*)(*)*; single and double bonds from the drawing are encoded explicitly in SMILES. Choose the substituted carbon as the SMILES root and attach the fragments as branches to obtain *C(C=C)(CC=C)O[Si](*)(*)*.
